analysis.investment_thesis: Jupiter is a genuine fast-grower in India's under-penetrated hospital sector — 22% revenue CAGR and expanding margins tell a clean story. But at P/E 43.5 with net profit growth decelerating sharply to ~10% in FY2025, you're paying a PEG north of 2.0, which violates my core discipline of buying growth at a reasonable price.
key_strengths: Revenue compounding at 22.2% CAGR over 5 years in a structurally underpenetrated Indian hospital market
Finance costs collapsed from INR 44 Cr (2022) to INR 11 Cr (2025) — debt paydown via IPO materially boosts future EPS
Operating margin expanding (16.89%) with gross margins of 63.4% — strong unit economics per bed
key_risks: Net profit growth decelerated hard — only 9.6% in FY2025 (INR 177→194 Cr), making PEG ~4.5x on trailing growth, well above my 1.0 threshold
Heavy capex cycle: INR 321 Cr spent in FY2025 with CWIP ballooning to INR 296 Cr — FCF turned negative (-67 Cr); new capacity ROI is unproven
Borrowings restarted at INR 403 Cr after being zeroed in FY2024 — execution risk if new hospitals ramp slower than expected
red_flags: PEG ratio >2.0 on any reasonable forward growth assumption — Lynch's hard ceiling is 1.5
FCF negative in FY2025 despite strong OCF — capex intensity could persist 2-3 more years before payoff
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Jupiter fits a classic hospital roll-up story I'd normally love — visible business, India's rising middle class demanding tertiary care, and a brand building real equity in western Mumbai. Revenue went from INR 463 Cr (2020) to INR 1,262 Cr (2025), and EBITDA margins held steady around 24-25%. The IPO proceeds wisely zeroed out debt in FY2024, and finance costs dropping from INR 44 Cr to INR 11 Cr will act as a multi-year EPS tailwind. The CWIP surge to INR 296 Cr tells me new beds are coming — this is where the next earnings leg lives.

The problem is price. At P/E 43.5, the market has already priced in the expansion. Net profit grew just 9.6% in FY2025 — a dramatic deceleration after the COVID-recovery spike. My PEG calculation: 43.5 divided by even an optimistic 20% forward earnings growth rate gives 2.17 — I want below 1.0 on fast growers, and 1.5 is my absolute ceiling. The stock needs either a 25-30% price correction or 2-3 years of 30%+ earnings growth to become interesting. I'd put this on my watchlist at INR 900-1,000 where the story gets compelling, but I won't chase it at current levels.
